FROM ARTWORK TO SAMPLE APPROVAL

Four steps. A considered print.

Follow the artwork, screen, print and sample decisions behind a spot-colour cup project.

Review the process with your artwork →

Artwork & spot colours

Prepare vector artwork, separate the design into spot colours and agree the print size and colour reference.

Vector artwork · Colour reference
01 / 04

Screen & cup positioning

Prepare a screen for each colour. Support the cup with a suitable fixture and align the stencil to the agreed print area.

Mesh stencil · Cup fixture
02 / 04

Squeegee & print

A squeegee pushes ink through the open stencil onto the supported cup. Additional colours require separate registered passes.

Squeegee · Mesh-to-cup contact
03 / 04

Cure & sample review

Use the curing conditions specified for the selected ink and substrate. Review registration, edges, appearance and adhesion against the agreed sample criteria.

Print edges · Appearance & adhesion
04 / 04

SPECIFICATIONS & SAMPLE REVIEW

Define the print before production.

ColoursSpot colours; screen count and colour reference confirmed with artwork.
Print areaModel-specific. Review taper, rim, seams and fixture clearance.
Substrate & inkConfirm the actual material, surface preparation and compatible ink system.
Curing & adhesionAgree curing conditions and test method on production samples.
Care & durabilityConfirm care instructions and any wash or rub test requirements separately.
MOQ & timingQuoted for the model, colour count, artwork, quantity and packing.

BEST FOR

Spot-colour logos
Clear lettering & bold shapes
Event and promotional cup artwork

BUYER QUESTIONS

Screen printing, explained.

Which artwork works well for screen printing?

Solid spot-colour logos, lettering and clear shapes are a useful starting point. Fine detail, minimum line width and registration must be reviewed at the actual print size.

Can screen printing reproduce photographs or gradients?

Photographic and continuous-tone artwork requires a separate process review. Compare UV printing or heat transfer when the brief needs detailed multicolour imagery.

How many colours can I use?

Each colour normally requires its own screen and registration. The practical colour count depends on the selected cup, artwork, ink and production setup; confirm it in the quotation.

How is print durability confirmed?

Agree the substrate, ink system, curing conditions, care instructions and any required tests. Approve an actual sample rather than assuming a wash-cycle rating.

What should I send for a quotation?

Send the model or reference image, vector artwork, colour reference, print location, quantity, packaging, destination and required arrival date. Request screen and setup charges as separate quote items.
